findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed donning gloves without handwashing. Education was carried out. Appropriate handwashing procedures were followed. Ensure that staff remember to always wash their hands before donning gloves.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Inspector observed three cans of tomatoes, one can of olive, and one can of pineapple dented in the middle of the can shelving. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were removed. Ensure that food items with compromised package integrity are removed from the inventory and returned appropriately.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. An accumulation of soil build up was observed on the shelvings use to hold dishes above the triple sink. 
2. The coving tiles under the steam table, triple sink, and the wall in front of the refrigerator by the kitchen entrance were observed coming off the wall.  
PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant action will be taken. Ensure that corrective actions are taken providing a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: Three cans of split black olives were observed dented in the middle of the can shelf. PIC was made aware. The dented cans were removed. Ensure that food items with compromised package integrity are removed from the inventory and returned appropriately.
findings.citation_text: 3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Raw shell eggs were observed being stored directly above cooked lasagna in the large standing refrigerator at the beginning of the cook line. PIC was made aware. The raw shell eggs were removed and stored properly. Ensure that food items are stored properly at all times to avoid cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The ambient temperature within the triple doors standing cooler in the far back of the kitchen was observed  higher than 41F. The average surface temperature collected was 57F. The recorded probing temperatures were 45F and 44F. PIC was made aware. PIC stated added an additional hanging thermometer into the unit. The food items were removed from the unit and placed in another unit. 
Ensure that this unit is repaired appropriately to avoid food spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a container of white powder under the prep table by the pizza dough mixer. The powder was later identified as flour. PIC was made aware. The container was labeled immediately. Ensure that white powders placed in containers other than their original containers are labeled properly at all times.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed the following food being stored in cans in the prep cooler.
1. Black olives were observed being stored in an opened can in the prep cooler.
2. Mackerels as per PIC were opened the day before was observed stored in the can in the prep cooler.

PIC was made aware. The food items mentioned were removed and placed in appropriate containers for proper storage. Ensure that can food when opened are place in appropriate containers to avoid botulism contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.14 Food Preparation. During preparation, unPACKAGED FOOD shall be protected from environmental sources of contamination.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
The following were observed. 
1. The internal surface of the microwaves in the kitchen were observed with encrusted food particles and debris. PIC had the microwaves cleaned immediately. (COS)
2. Molded food particles were observed scatted in the bottom of the prep cooler. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the surface of the cooler bottom will be cleaned. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces such as the inside of the prep cooler bottom and microwaves are kept free of encrusted food deposits and soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(B) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: The gasket of the left door of the pizza prep cooler was observed loose. Discussed with PIC. PIC told inspector that a new gasket had been ordered. Ensure that the gasket is repaired ensuring that the door of the cooler is properly sealed to avoid food spoilage.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed .
1. The hoods covering the fan in the standing cooler were observed with an accumulation to soil and dust. 
2. Inspector observed accumulated soil and dust in multiple areas in the kitchen. PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the kitchen and all relevant areas will be cleaned. Ensure that the cleaning frequency of the kitchen is increase to avoid the accumulation of soil and dust.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify the food handler certification of a couple employees. PIC told inspector that they were unsure whether the employees had the certification or not. Ensure that all employees handling food are trained and certified. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
Inspector was unable to verify a valid allergen certification for the only certified food protection manager in the facility. PIC told inspector that they will look for the certification or get the training done. Ensure that the training is done to be in compliance with the law.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Inspector observed evidence of the hand sink at the bar being use as a dump sink. PIC was made aware about the hand sink serving only for the purpose of handwashing. The hand sink was created and staff was educated, Ensure that designated sinks for handwashing be use solely for handwashing and nothing else. 

Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels.

Paper towels are missing at multiple hand sinks throughout the facility. Sinks include: 1) in the bar area; 2) in the men’s bathroom and; 3) in the kitchen by the door. The PIC was shown and replaced the paper towels at each sink to correct. Ensure that each hand sink is always correctly supplied at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

A cup of water without lid/straw is observed on a shelf above the prep counter next to the stove. Cooked lasagna noodles are being prepped under this shelf. The PIC was shown and removed the cup to correct. Employee foods/drinks were discussed. Ensure that all employee stored food items do not provide a potential contamination source for RTE foods.

Ensure the soda holster is cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary to maintain it clean. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.comment:
4-602 Observed the interior of the ice bin in the bar to have a slight accumulation of soil. The identifying cap from the adjacent soda gun was observed fallen into the bottom of the ice bin and was stuck in the soil. Cleaning and sanitizing will be completed before opening later tonight. Keep ice bin covered to insure safe food. 
(A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours.

7-101.11: Containers of POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS and PERSONAL CARE ITEMS shall bear a legible manufacturer's label.
